question.text:
You are analyzing the annual returns of an equity fund over the past five years: Fund X: 8%, 12%, -5%, 15%, 10%
Calculate the arithmetic average annual return for Fund X.

explanation.text: The Logic: Arithmetic average = (sum of annual returns) / number of years. For Fund X: (8% + 12% − 5% + 15% + 10%) / 5 = 40% / 5 = 8%. The Trap: 8.5% tempts candidates who mis-add the series. 7.5% tempts those who treat the -5% as -10%. 9% tempts those who drop a period or round prematurely. All three distractors reward careless arithmetic. Note: The question is a plain arithmetic-average exercise. Time-weighted measures such as HPR, XIRR or TWRR (covered separately in the PMS workbook) would give a different number.
